title: A shallow tree, visible on three boards
summary: Keep the original safe. Explore a child on a second copy, then bring its refutation back one level at a time.
walkthrough: Copy the original and try 4 at r3c3. Lightning reaches another Dilemma.
Copy that position. At r1c3 the remaining choices are 3 and 6. Trying 3 produces a contradiction.
Overlay the child on its parent. Remove 3 from that parent, then tap the child thumbnail to unstack it. The remaining choice, 6, leads through forced moves to another contradiction.
Both child alternatives have failed, so the assumption r3c3 = 4 is impossible. Overlay its board on the original, remove that 4 there, and use Lightning to finish the puzzle.

title: One board: a failed guess, a replay, and a solution
summary: Use the fill disc to revisit a failed guess, inspect it with Redo, and solve on one board with Lightning.
walkthrough: The starting candidates at r1c2 are 1, 6 and 7. Try 1, then let Lightning follow the forced moves to a warning.
Two-finger double-tap Undo returns to Dilemma. The dashed disc identifies the tried 1. Three-finger double-tap Redo lets you inspect that same failed path; Undo returns to its decision again.
Remove 1 with the direction wheel. Next try 7; Lightning also reaches a contradiction. Backtrack to its fill disc and remove 7.
Only 6 remains at r1c2. Lightning follows that forced fill and all its consequences to a solved grid. No copied board is used.

title: Follow the ring back to the founding fill
summary: A note ring is not the founding fill. Continue smart Undo until the disc locates the assumption whose whole subtree failed.
walkthrough: Try 6 at r2c3. Lightning follows its consequences to a Dilemma where r2c9 has 3 or 8.
Try 8. After Lightning reaches a warning, smart Undo identifies its fill disc. Remove 8 in this conditional position; the remaining 3 also leads to a contradiction.
Smart Undo now shows a ring for the note removal. Both child alternatives have failed. Continue double-tap Undo until the disc identifies the earlier r2c3 = 6 assumption.
Inspect the saved path with Redo before changing it. Undo back to that disc, then remove 6 at the original decision. You are at another Dilemma, ready to continue the search.
